subject.title: Interactive parity with the Codex runtime: ask-user-question · plan mode · goal mode — the roadmap

question: Should OpenClaw accept Codex-style structured questions, plan mode, and goal-mode continuation in core now, and should the linked implementation land as one branch or be split by feature group?
rationale: The request changes core runtime behavior, gateway protocol/UI surfaces, channel delivery, tool exposure, and unattended goal semantics, so automation cannot choose the release shape or product boundary safely.

options.title: Split staged PRs
options.body: Review and land the question pipeline, plan mode, and goal driver as separate focused changes with proof for each surface.

options.title: Sponsor full branch
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the broad review cost and own the linked PR as a bundled interactive-parity rollout after proof and CI are resolved.

options.title: Defer or narrow
options.body: Maintainers can keep the roadmap open but reject or defer parts that should wait for a smaller plugin/API or security design.

recommendation.title: Split staged PRs
recommendation.body: Review and land the question pipeline, plan mode, and goal driver as separate focused changes with proof for each surface.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal on update_plan exposure and strict-agentic execution policy, which are central to the product decision.
